newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB 4.6% bond due Nov '97 traded at 6.1%--traders.
newsitem.headline: NCB 4.6% bond due Nov '97 traded at 6.1%--traders.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd's (NCB) 4.6 percent five-year bank debenture due in November 1997 was traded at 6.1 percent on Monday, traders said.
One billion yen worth of the debentures changed hands, a trader for a major brokerage house said.
The market yield was about 10 basis points higher than Friday's rate, the trader said.
Market yields of NCB's debentures have shown little sign of declining recently, traders said.

"Some NCB debentures have yields of around six percent, but others are stuck with offers of around seven to eight percent. There are hardly any bids for the debentures," said a trader for a city bank's securities affiliate.
Traders said recent falls in NCB's share price were prompting selling of its debentures.
NCB shares have been falling on lingering uncertainty over the effectiveness of the long-term credit bank's restructuring plan, stockbrokers said.
NCB shares were down 19 yen at an all-time low of 171 as of 0211 GMT on Monday.
NCB announced a major restructuring plan on April 1 that will mean the loss of 600 jobs, the sale of prime real estate and a withdrawal from major overseas markets.
The bank said it believes the scheme will help it to regain the market's trust.
